title: Expenses Sky pays on a Prime's behalf become advances netted against its Genesis Capital Allocation
content:
A.2.8.2.2.2.7.4 makes the rule general: "Any operational or other expenses incurred by a Prime and paid directly by Sky after July 1, 2025 shall be treated as an advance against the Prime's Genesis Capital Allocation," documented and "deducted from the Prime's allocated capital funds at the time of the Capital Transfer."

A.2.8.2.2.2.7.2.1 shows it settled in practice. Against a 25 million USDS allocation (A.2.8.2.2.2.4.1), the transfer to the Spark SubProxy was 20.6 million, "reflect[ing] that 4.4 million USDS of pre-TGE expenses were paid by Sky" — 2 million to market makers and 2.4 million to exchanges, both from the Sky Ecosystem Liquidity Bootstrapping Budget.

The mechanism turns the genesis allocation into a **running account** rather than a grant. Sky can fund a Prime's needs as they arise, without a separate approval or a loan agreement each time, because every payment is automatically an advance against a number already agreed. That removes friction during exactly the period when a Prime has no treasury of its own.

It also settles the question of what Sky's early spending was: not a subsidy on top of the allocation, but a draw against it. Anyone reading the headline 25 million as the amount Spark received would be wrong by 18%.

The requirement that "the total amount of such expenses shall be documented" is the control that makes this safe for the Prime — the deduction is auditable rather than asserted at settlement. The same instinct appears elsewhere in this Accord: money moved early is remembered and netted later rather than forgiven.
description: Spark's 25 million USDS allocation was transferred as 20.6 million because 4.4 million of pre-TGE liquidity bootstrapping had already been paid by Sky and deducted at the Capital Transfer.
